blocks.text: localStorage is a synchronous per-origin string dictionary persisting across sessions. Structures must be JSON-serialized and validated on load because old code, users, or extensions may have changed them. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: A labeled drawer keeps cards between visits, but every retrieved card must be checked before use.

localStorage is a synchronous per-origin string dictionary persisting across sessions. Structures must be JSON-serialized and validated on load because old code, users, or extensions may have changed them. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

setItem stores only strings and may fail for quota/security; JSON.parse may throw SyntaxError. A namespaced versioned key permits migration or safe abandonment of old formats. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

Store neither secrets nor server truth; wrap reads/writes, limit size, validate every field, and provide a safe default on corruption. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

recap: Core idea: A complete widget maintains source state, derives its display, and exposes every transition through semantics, focus, and messages. Mouse, keyboard, and assistive technology trigger the same logic without duplication.
derived state: Value recalculable from a source.
live region: Region whose updates are announced.
progressive enhancement: Native function enhanced without losing its baseline.
